questions.question: 1. In a frequency reuse plan, what is the relationship between cells within the same cluster?

answers.a: They all use the exact same set of frequencies.
answers.b: They are all co-channel cells to each other.
answers.c: They each use a unique, separate set of frequencies.
answers.d: They must all use directional antennas.

questions.question: 2. Why is a hexagonal shape commonly used to represent cells in a cluster diagram?

answers.a: It perfectly represents the true radio signal coverage.
answers.b: It's the only shape that allows for frequency reuse.
answers.c: It tessellates to cover an area completely without gaps or overlaps.
answers.d: It ensures that co-channel interference is always zero.

questions.question: 3. What does the term 'cluster size' refer to?

answers.a: The physical land area covered by a single cluster.
answers.b: The total number of users a cluster can support.
answers.c: The number of cells in a single cluster.
answers.d: The number of co-channel cells in the network.

questions.question: 4. If a system designer chooses a cluster size of seven, what does this mean?

answers.a: The entire available frequency spectrum is divided into seven sets.
answers.b: There are seven co-channel cells for every cell.
answers.c: Each cell can only talk to seven other cells.
answers.d: The system can only support seven users at a time.

questions.question: 5. What is the primary limiting factor that prevents using a cluster size of one (where all cells use all frequencies)?

answers.b: High cost of base station equipment

questions.question: 6. In a frequency reuse pattern, how many 'first-tier' co-channel cells typically surround a center cell?

answers.d: It depends on the cluster size.

questions.question: 7. A network operator wants to increase the capacity in a dense urban area. What change to the cluster size would help achieve this?

answers.c: Keep the cluster size the same but increase tower height.
answers.d: Use a cluster size of zero.

questions.question: 8. What is the main negative consequence of decreasing the cluster size to improve capacity?

answers.a: A decrease in the total number of channels available.
answers.c: A larger physical footprint for each cell.
answers.d: A reduction in the number of handoffs.

questions.question: 9. The 'frequency reuse factor' is inversely related to what parameter?
10. What is the purpose of 'tessellating' or repeating the cell cluster pattern?

answers.a: To ensure every user has the same signal strength.
answers.b: To provide continuous coverage over a large service area.
answers.c: To reduce the number of base stations needed.
answers.d: To eliminate all adjacent channel interference.
